newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin creates body to improve tax collection.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin creates body to improve tax collection.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin said in a radio address on Friday that he had created a special commission to improve tax collection under the leadership of Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
Criticising Russia's poor record of tax collection in a brief address, he said the emergency commission would take control of the work of the customs and tax services.

Yeltsin spoke clearly in the address, apparently recorded in the sanatorium where he is preparing for heart surgery in the next two months. He said the deputy head of the commission would be Anatoly Chubais, the Kremlin chief of staff.
"The commission will be called extraordinary because the situation in this sphere can be described only as extraordinary," the 65-year-old president said.

He made clear better tax collection was intended to help pay off a huge backlog of wages to workers who are paid by the state, including servicemen, and to pay overdue pensions. He vowed to punish tax collectors and others who worked badly.
"I can assure pensioners and the workers in the budget sphere -- policemen and servicemen -- that pensions and salaries will be paid. I, as the president, am confident of it," he said.
